ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's list of designated terrorists. Enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), including family members and close associates. Continuous monitoring via automated screening tools and quarterly manual reviews. For customs brokerage, additional screening against the General Administration of Customs (GACC) blacklist and the Ministry of Commerce's export control lists. All screening results must be documented, risk-rated, and escalated to the AML Compliance Officer for approval. Any positive hit requires immediate suspension of the incorporation process and filing of a suspicious transaction report with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Information Publicity System (NECP) and the local SAMR online name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters. For foreign investors, the name may include a transliteration of the foreign name. The name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive name + industry/activity + legal form (e.g., 'Limited Liability'). The distinctive name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Phonetic transliteration is permitted but must use approved Chinese characters. The name must not contain any prohibited or sensitive tokens without prior ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the local SAMR within 60 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written statement explaining why the name is not confusingly similar, supported by evidence of prior search results or trademark registration. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court within 6 months. The entire process typically takes 30-60 days. It is advisable to engage local counsel to prepare the appeal and to consider alternative name options to expedite the process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not permissible for customs brokerage activities. The local tax authorities and banks require a physical office address with a lease agreement, utility bills, and evidence of actual business operations. The General Administration of Customs (GACC) mandates a registered business address and may conduct on-site inspections. A virtual office would fail the commercial substance test and jeopardize the customs brokerage license application.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Lease agreement in the company's name; (2) Utility bills (electricity, water) matching the registered address; (3) Presence of office furniture, equipment, and staff during business hours; (4) Compliance with fire safety regulations; (5) Availability of business records and customs brokerage documentation. Risk: High likelihood of unannounced inspections by the local SAMR and GACC, especially within the first 12 months of operation. Quantified risk: 70% probability of at least one physical inspection within the first year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 9, 23, 26, 30, 40, 42, 46, 47, 68 and 76; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 3, 18, 22 and 30; Customs Law of the People's Republic of China (2021 Amendment), Articles 27, 28 and 30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) in the district/county of the registered office; the Ministry of Commerce is notified via the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Reporting System for foreign-invested enterprise filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application (Form SAMR A-1) together with the Company's Articles of Association and the 'Non-foreign-investment Negative List Compliance Confirmation' filed under the Foreign Investment Information Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The PRC Company Law (2023) abolished any minimum registered capital for ordinary limited liability companies. The WFOE may subscribe any amount of registered capital, but all subscribed capital must be fully paid-in within five years from issuance of the business license. If the customs brokerage engages in bonded transit guarantee operations, the customs authority may require a bond or guarantee amount based on the value of the customs duties, but no minimum paid-up capital of the company is prescribed. The incorporators must execute a capital contribution schedule and deposit the initial contribution to an escrow-like account only to the extent required by the customs authority for the customs broker bond.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
THE FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS (WRITTEN RESOLUTION) OF [•] CO., LTD. (THE 'COMPANY') ADOPTED ON THE [•] DAY OF [•], 2025.

WHEREAS: (A) The Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in the People's Republic of China; (B) The incorporator has executed the Articles of Association and all pre-incorporation agreements; and (C) The sole director and the supervisors of the Company have received the capital contribution undertaking and the financial projection of the customs brokerage house.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY HEREBY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE. The board acknowledges that the initial registered capital of the Company is [•] RMB/USD, divided into [•] ordinary shares of [•] each. The shareholders' subscriptions are approved and the board directs the issue of capital contribution certificates upon receipt of each installment. All capital contributions shall be paid into a bank account opened in the Company's name within the statutory five-year period and shall be applied solely to the lawful business of the Company as a licensed customs declaration and brokerage enterprise.

2. BANKING AND TREASURY AUTHORIZATION. The board selects [•] Bank, [•] branch, as the principal bank of the Company. The chairperson and the general manager, jointly or singly in amounts below USD 20,000 and jointly for amounts above, are authorized to open a basic deposit account, a foreign exchange capital account, a general account, and an online banking module. The bank mandate cards and the specimen signature lists are approved and filed with the board minutes.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The board formally adopts the premises located at [•] floor, [•] House, [•] Street, [•] District, [•] Municipality, China, as the Company's statutory registered office and principal place of business. The general manager is authorized to execute the lease agreement, pay the security deposit, cause the lease filing with the housing regulation authority, and obtain the building fire and safety documents required for the customs license.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints [•] as the legal representative and chairperson, [•] as general manager, [•] as responsible person for customs operations, [•] as chief financial officer, and [•] as the supervisor. Each officer accepts the appointment and confirms they shall exercise due diligence, avoid conflicts of interest, and discharge out-of-office statutory duties in accordance with PRC law. The supervisor shall not act as an executive officer concurrently.

5. CUSTOMS REGISTRATION AND GOVERNANCE FILINGS. The board directs the general manager to submit the Company's business license, office lease, the certificate of the customs affairs principal, and the organisation chart to the General Administration of Customs and its local district customs. The board further authorizes the execution of the customs broker registration application, the customs declaration system purchase agreement, and any environmental registration or fire safety documentation required for the premises.

6. FINAL AUTHORIZATION AND POWER TO WIND UP. Any two officers, one of whom must be the legal representative, are jointly authorized to execute, submit, and file all necessary instruments, to make amendments to non-material items requested by any government registry, and to participate in any inquiry or supplement process issued by the SAMR, the tax authority, or the customs authority. This written resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minute book and exhibited to third parties as evidence of the authority of the officers.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this resolution is in full force and effect until revoked by an express subsequent resolution of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Negative-List Business Scope Vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the online Enterprise Integration Registration Platform at https://www.gsxt.gov.cn
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit name reservation application for the proposed Chinese and English company name, with the shareholder as the foreign parent and the word 'Customs Brokerage' in the scope. The platform checks duplicate and identical names against the national registry and applies the prohibited list for foreign investment. Legal counsel must verify that ISIC 5229 services fall under the permitted 'transport auxiliary activities' of the Foreign Investment Negative List. After approval, a reservation number is issued and the applicant has six months to file the establishment application. Any change of business scope before filing requires a new name reservation.
required_dossiers: Reserved company name and reservation number
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent company
Passport or corporate identity proof of the proposed legal representative
Letter of authorization from the foreign parent appointing the local signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to identical name, file an objection with the same SAMR within 15 days; alternatively submit three priority alternative names in the same session, which resets the review clock to three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization and Translation of Parent and Individual Credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the place of incorporation of the foreign parent; Chinese consulate if Apostille not applicable; a PRC licensed translation service engaged by counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All corporate documents of the parent, including its certificate of good standing, board resolution on incorporation of the WFOE, power of attorney for the local incorporator, and financial solvency statement, must be apostilled in the parent's jurisdiction. Under the Hague Apostille Convention as implemented in China, no consular legalization is required for member states, but the apostille certificate must be fresh, not older than six months. The Chinese translation must be produced by a translation company licensed in China and the translation package must include the translator's seal and the declaration of accuracy. The same translation requirements apply to the passport and address proof of the legal representative.
required_dossiers: Apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent
Apostilled certificate of good standing (issued within 3 months)
Apostilled parent board resolution approving the WFOE
Notarized POA for the local signatory
Official Chinese translation of all above plus translator license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the apostille is rejected as insufficient, return the document to the source notary and re-issue a standardized apostille with the correct Hague Convention form. If translation is rejected, commission a second licensed translator and submit within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Registration Filing and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (District/County MSA) in the intended registered office district.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment pack with the designated MSA online or physically. The application includes the authenticated parent documents, the signed Articles of Association, the lease agreement for the office premises, proof of seating and office address, the appointment documents for the legal representative, supervisor, and manager, and the shareholder subscription list. The MSA will issue an electronic receipt and afterwards either the business license or a supplement requirement notice. Once the license is issued, the company automatically obtains social credit code and taxpayer identification; the license copy must be kept at the registered office together with the company seal. The registration fee is zero, but the company must pay the stamp duty of 0.025% on paid-in capital at the time of actual contribution.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form (SAMR A-1)
Signed Articles of Association
Lease agreement and address certificate for the registered office
Appointment letters for legal representative, supervisor, and manager
Apostilled/notarized parent documents (incorporated package)
Shareholder subscription list with capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a supplementary materials notice is issued, the applicant has 15 natural days to submit the missing items; if not cured on time, the application is considered abandoned and a new application with a new name reservation may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Engraving, Public Security Filing and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR-licensed seal engraving enterprise and Public Security Bureau (seal filing registry); the bank of the Company's selection.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the license is obtained, the legal representative must personally attend the seal engraving station or provide a notarized authorization. The following seals are required: company seal, legal representative seal, financial seal, invoice seal and contract seal. The engraving station files each seal's specimen with the Public Security Bureau. With the license and seals, the company opens the basic deposit account, foreign exchange capital account and general account at the chosen bank. The foreign exchange account registration must be filed with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the bank. Bank account opening is precondition for any paid-in capital contribution and for the customs broker guarantee bond.
required_dossiers: Business license (original and copies)
Legal representative identity certificate
Seal engraving authorization/POA
Taxpayer identification notice and tax registration evidence
Bank required documents including Articles of Association and seal specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal filing fails due to missing statutory documents, the legal representative must correct the registry record and apply for a police verification certificate within 3 working days. For bank account refusal, choose another bank and resubmit within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Labor Registration and Customs Declaration Enterprise Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; General Administration of Customs (GACC) district customs office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the taxpayer registration through the online 'New Taxpayer Startup Package' by linking the social credit code. Register social insurance, housing fund, and employment filing at the local HRSS and housing fund center. For the customs brokerage, file the 'Customs Declaration Enterprise Registration' with the local customs via the GACC single window, upload the business license, the lease, the list of at least two certified customs declaration personnel, the operations procedure manual, and the guarantee bond or guarantee insurance policy. Customs shall grant approval within ten working days and assign a customs enterprise code. After that, the enterprise may connect to the Automated Broker Interface through a licensed EDI vendor. If the company also intends to handle bonded transit, the customs authority will inspect the warehousing premises and may impose a non-intrusive monitoring system.
required_dossiers: Business license with customs-related business scope
Lease contract and premises certificate
Customs declaration enterprise registration form (GACC Form G-1)
Employment contracts and qualifications of customs clearance staff
Guarantee bond or guarantee insurance policy
Operations procedures and systems manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the customs registration is rejected for insufficient guarantee or untrained staff, cure the defects by increasing the guarantee bond and enrolling the staff through the GACC training system, then reapply within 20 days. If customs demands an environmental or fire revision, complete the remediation order and submit a compliance report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Administration of Customs (GACC) of the People's Republic of China; local Customs District; Ministry of Emergency Management (for fire safety); local Ecology and Environment Bureau (for environmental registration if applicable).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration Certificate for Customs Declaration Enterprise (customs broker registration) issued by GACC under the Customs Declaration Enterprise Registration Measures; business license must include the item 'customs agency, bonded transit and freight brokerage'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the local Ecology and Environment Bureau of the district of the registered office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Category III) for office-based customs brokerage with no physical manufacturing or warehousing; if ancillary bonded warehousing of less than 5,000 square meters is included, an Environmental Impact Registration Form is sufficient; if warehousing exceeds 5,000 square meters or involves hazardous chemicals, a full Environmental Impact Report (Category I) is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only: no industrial wastewater; domestic sewage to municipal network must meet GB/T 31962-2015 with CODcr ≤ 500 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, SS ≤ 400 mg/L, NH3-N ≤ 45 mg/L; if adjunct warehouse, boundary non-methane total hydrocarbons (NMHC) fugitive concentration ≤ 2.0 mg/m3 and leak detection per GB 37822-2019; hazardous waste generated in small quantities must be collected in leak-proof containers and transferred to a licensed treatment facility with a manifest within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Acceptance Certificate ('Fire Check Acceptance Form') from the local Fire and Rescue Brigade for the leased office, plus a building structural safety certificate or owner's warranty for the floor loading if any racking or bonded storage is installed; occupational workplace safety clearance from the local Emergency Management Bureau, requiring an emergency evacuation plan, fire extinguisher installations, staff first-aid and fire-fighting training records, and a written occupational health management system.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); local competent tax office in the city/district of registration; online filing portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) accessible via the STA main portal www.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE is first registered with the State Administration for Market Regulation and receives an 18-character Unified Social Credit Code, which is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN); no separate VAT identification number is issued. The WFOE must complete tax registration confirmation on the Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days of the business license date, supplementing the registration with the legal representative, financial officer, tax agent, registered and operating address, bank account details, accounting standards, and chosen VAT taxpayer status. The STA then activates the tax account. A foreign non-resident shareholder is not automatically registered for Chinese tax; if the non-resident has China-source income or a permanent establishment, it must complete non-resident enterprise taxpayer registration on the same e-Tax platform and obtain a non-resident taxpayer identification before performing any tax filings or withholding certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box elections or hybrid-mismatch elections. A WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Voluntary VAT general taxpayer registration is available for small-scale taxpayers but is only an indirect tax status election, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Basic VAT registration has no economic turnover threshold; all Chinese enterprises, including a WFOE, must complete tax registration within 30 days of obtaining the business license. Compulsory registration as a VAT general taxpayer applies when annual VAT taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000; below that, small-scale taxpayer status applies. Customs brokerage and logistics auxiliary services are taxed under the 6% VAT service category, while the 13% headline rate applies to goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires all VAT invoices to be issued through the STA-controlled Electronic Invoice Service Platform using the fully digitalized electronic invoice mechanism or authorized tax-control equipment. Invoice data is transmitted in real time to the STA Golden Tax system, and each invoice carries a statutorily generated 20-digit invoice number and anti-counterfeit QR code. Taxpayers perform invoice receipt, verification, and reconciliation in the Tax Digital Account. Customs electronic export data is automatically connected to the tax system; no separate fiscal stamping is required before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, the 0% export VAT rate/export rebate is available where the exporter is a VAT general taxpayer, the goods are physically exported, the customs declaration is authenticated by China Customs, and export proceeds are repatriated within the required foreign-exchange period. The rebate is applied under the exemption-credit-refund method for manufacturing/exporting producers or the exemption-refund method for trading exporters. For taxable services, zero-rating/exemption applies only to qualifying cross-border services supplied to a non-resident recipient and wholly consumed outside China; customs declaration and brokerage services physically performed at Chinese ports do not by themselves qualify. Bonded transit and customs-supervised zone services may be treated under special regime rules and should be confirmed through a written determination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration generated through the China International Trade Single Window and released by China Customs
Export contract or sales order and packing list
Commercial invoice and, for trading exporters, the VAT Special Invoice for the purchased goods
Transport document such as Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or Post Receipt evidencing goods leaving Chinese customs territory
Bank foreign exchange receipt voucher recorded in the SAFE Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System evidencing the inward remittance of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA cross-checks export zero-rating against China Customs release data and SAFE foreign-exchange collection data. If documentation, export, or repatriation is incomplete or false, the STA may claw back refunded VAT, void the zero-rating, assess VAT at the applicable rate, impose late-payment surcharge, and impose administrative penalties of 50% to 5 times the tax evaded under Article 63 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Levy and Collection of the People's Republic of China. Fraudulent export refund claims may be prosecuted as the crime of export tax refund fraud under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and SAFE may separately penalize failure to repatriate export proceeds or falsification of foreign-exchange receipt records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a bifurcated current-account and capital-account convertibility framework. Current-account transactions, including trade-related payments and dividends that have been properly verified with supporting documents, are generally classified as convertible, subject to documentary review and reporting by SAFE and its designated foreign exchange banks. Capital-account transactions, by contrast, require prior SAFE registration or approval: inbound foreign direct investment through a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise must be registered under the SAFE FDI rules, the capital contribution must be paid into a foreign-currency capital account, and any subsequent conversion into RMB must occur in a transaction-specific manner with the proceeds recorded in a use ledger. Profit and dividend remittances are treated as current-account transfers but are not automatic: the WFOE must present audited financial statements, a board resolution approving the distribution, a tax withholding certificate or tax clearance certificate, and proof of no outstanding foreign-exchange control violations. In practice, banks require the remittance to be made net of withholding taxes and will reject payment orders if the supporting audit and tax documentation is stale or inconsistent. Export proceeds enjoy broadly convertible current-account treatment, but the same flows remain subject to trade verification, invoice matching, and monitoring ratios set by SAFE to prevent disguised capital flows and trade-based money laundering. The WFOE must therefore maintain a robust treasury and compliance framework to navigate periodic macro-prudential adjustments to capital-flow management operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts must be repatriated through a designated foreign exchange bank and reported via the SAFE cross-border receipt confirmation system. For standard exports, the exporter must ensure that payment confirmation occurs within the prescribed 90-day trade collection period from the date of exportation, extendable to 180 days for certain qualifying high-technology and advanced-manufacturing goods. There is no universal mandatory conversion ratio applicable to all export proceeds; the WFOE may retain foreign currency within its SAFE-approved current-account foreign exchange quota, and any balance above the authorised retention quota must be settled into RMB promptly at the prevailing onshore spot rate. One hundred percent of proceeds must be evidenced, accounted for, and matched to underlying customs declarations; unreconciled overdue receipts will trigger a compliance investigation, downgrade of trade facilitation status, and possible suspension of the customs duty payment and collection interface.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic-money institutions and digital EMI platforms have low standalone viability in Mainland China. They are not licensed to accept deposits or provide local clearing accounts as primary settlement rails for a WFOE under PRC banking supervision and foreign exchange control law. Such EMIs may operate only as technology or customer-acquisition partners to onshore Tier-1 banks, and they are legally barred from acting as the formal banking channel for capital injections, customs duty payments, or export receipt collection. Any cross-border disbursement initiated by an offshore EMI without an onshore licensed partner bank would be rejected by SAFE as an unregistered payment flow. The WFOE should therefore rely on traditional Chinese commercial banks for settlement and clearing, and may use global EMI platforms solely for utility-type expense payments outside China, subject to bank approval and a clear audit trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Chinese banking regulations and standard onboarding practice require the WFOE legal representative and at least one director with signing authority to appear physically at the designated branch for the account-opening interview and on-site KYC verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not an absolute right; it is permitted only where a domestic banking institution legally permits remote or offshore origination channels, and even then the bank must complete a video interview, a notarised and consularised or apostilled power of attorney, passport certification, source-of-funds evidence, and a board resolution. Given the enhanced risk profile of a licensed customs brokerage house under a foreign-owned structure, the prudent recommendation is an in-person opening at a Tier-1 bank branch in the registered jurisdiction. Any deviation from physical presence materially lengthens the compliance review period and frequently triggers a secondary AML review, so the treasury team should plan for an executive travel mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign equity ownership with opaque chain-of-custody or nominee shareholding arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts covering every entity in the ownership chain, notarised passport copies of all natural-person shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners holding over 25%, a board resolution in both English and Chinese confirming no nominee arrangements, and a European or Hong Kong bank reference letter supporting the source of funds and professional standing of the ultimate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs brokerage business exposing the account to trade-based money laundering red flags such as inconsistent HS codes or shipment values
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid PRC Customs Brokerage Licence, business scope endorsement from the authority, a projected transaction flow chart showing client onboarding, declaration processes and payment flows, a sample of ten historical client files with commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations and documentary export evidence, and a written AML compliance manual incorporating customer risk rating, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration risk from a single high-risk jurisdiction or an unusually high volume of third-party payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed client and supplier matrix evidencing commercial rationale for each counterparty, contractual agreements for each high-value relationship, transport and customs declaration documents corroborating each transaction, sanctions/PEP/negative-news screening reports from a recognised professional database, and a written explanation of the expected transaction footprint with annual thresholds and monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from a jurisdiction on the Financial Action Task Force or internal bank high-risk list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth affidavit on the ultimate beneficial owner, three months of bank statements from the remitting institution, underlying merger or establishment agreements evidencing the bona fide investment, tax residency certificates from the origin and destination jurisdictions, and a certified legal opinion confirming the corporate structure is not designed for money-laundering or tax evasion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas shareholder to the WFOE's foreign-currency capital account opened at the designated onshore bank. The remittance instruction must align with the SAFE FDI registration certificate and include the standard foreign-exchange payment purpose code for inward direct investment in China. Upon receipt, the onshore bank completes the cross-border banking statistics and payment confirmation, after which the WFOE may convert the capital funds into RMB in compliance with the transaction-realisation principle and transfer into a separate RMB capital funds expenditure account. A qualified Chinese certified public accountant must perform capital verification and issue a capital verification report before the funds can be used for customs brokerage operations, bonded deposits, customs duty advances or general working capital; any use outside the SAFE-approved negative-list scope is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For effective trade settlements, the WFOE should operate through the following rails: direct SWIFT MT103 payments to overseas customs authorities, bondsmen, carriers and licensees for non-documentary operational costs; commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued by the onshore bank for high-value logistics or brokerage services where the counterparty demands documentary security; documentary collections in the form of documents against payment (D/P) and documents against acceptance (D/A) for low-risk recurring transactions; and the China Customs Single Window system connected to the bank-enterprise tripartite direct debit interface for the payment of import duties, VAT and other customs charges. All outbound payments must be supported by the relevant customs declaration, invoice, contract and tax declaration records, and each transaction must be submitted through the bank's current-account FX payment screening system before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB foreign exchange forward contracts with commercial banks for hedging trade receivables and payables, subject to documented current-account trade exposure
RMB/FX foreign exchange swaps and cross-currency basis swaps for liquidity management on approved capital flows, provided they are linked to actual transaction requirements and not speculative
Plain-vanilla currency options and option combinations with qualified onshore banks, fully supported by underlying trade documentation and approved by SAFE

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for mainland-resident corporate entities; such instruments may only be executed by overseas counterparty entities outside the SAFE jurisdiction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (年度报告公示) submitted by Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 to June 30 covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; failure to rectify within 3 years leads to inclusion in the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, administrative penalty up to RMB 10,000, and potential revocation of business license by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Filing and Settlement (企业所得税汇算清缴)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) – local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 to May 31 following the end of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; serious non-compliance may trigger tax audit, asset freeze, and restrictions on legal representative exit from China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Brokerage Annual Inspection / Annual Filing Renewal (报关企业年度备案)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Administration of Customs of China (GACC) via the Customs Enterprise Import-Export Credit System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before March 31 for changes; filing confirmation must be maintained effective throughout the year; annual maintenance report due by June 30 for customs broker records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain valid customs registration will lead to suspension of the customs brokerage license, inability to process customs declarations, potential downgrade of credit status, and administrative fines under the Customs Supervision Regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Report (外商投资信息报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via integrated market regulation platform; shares data with SAMR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and June 30 covering the previous calendar year, submitted with the Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or false submission triggers administrative corrective order, fine up to RMB 500,000, and negative credit record affecting future foreign exchange and government incentive eligibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Exchange Annual Inspection (直接投资存量权益登记) for Foreign-Invested Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through banks or the SAFE service platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 to June 30 for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report results in the entity being placed under foreign exchange business restriction; the enterprise cannot perform foreign exchange settlement or payment for cross-border transactions; repeated violations trigger fines up to RMB 300,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return for Value-Added Tax (including customs agency services subject to VAT) and Additional Surcharges
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) – local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns due by the 15th day of the following period; annual VAT reconciliation due May 31 if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing daily penalty of RMB 50 per return; monthly late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day; continuous delinquency can trigger tax authority compulsory collection, bank account freeze, and disqualification on customs broker license renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax (IIT) Monthly/Annually Withheld Return for Employees and Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) – local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or withholding period returns by the 15th day; annual comprehensive income settlement for employees due March 31 of the following year (employer coordination) / June 30 for individuals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of 50% to 5 times of the underpaid or unpaid tax; daily overdue interest of 0.05%; severe cases impose restrictions on legal representative credit and denial of customs AEO certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statistical/Industry Reporting (规模以上企业统计报表) if revenue or headcount thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) via local statistics bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly and annual; annual final report due March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit triggers warning and fine up to RMB 50,000; persistent non-reporting may affect enterprise credit classification and eligibility for government administrative services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Registration Certificate Renewal / Annual Relationship Maintenance (海关备案信息年度确认)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Administration of Customs of China (GACC) – local customs office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every year, the customs authority automatically reviews the enterprise filing information; a written confirmation must be made within the annual reporting cycle by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the filing information becomes invalid or inactive, customs clearance privileges are suspended; the entity is removed from the active customs broker list until re-registration and may receive a warning or fine up to RMB 100,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises in China are statutorily required to undergo an annual independent audit of their financial statements by a licensed Chinese Certified Public Accountant (CPA) firm, regardless of revenue, asset, or headcount size. The audit is mandated under the Accounting Law, the Company Law, and the Foreign Investment Law. Enterprises subject to compulsory annual audit include all limited liability companies with foreign investment, customs brokerage license holders, and any entity meeting any of the following: total assets exceeding RMB 50 million; annual turnover exceeding RMB 30 million; or headcount exceeding 300 employees. Additionally, customs brokerage houses with an annual volume exceeding 10,000 customs declaration entries or those applying for AEO (Authorized Economic Operator) certification are independently audited for customs compliance. Audit and reporting must be prepared in accordance with the Chinese Accounting Standards (ASBE / CAS) which are substantially converged with IFRS; enterprises with listed shares or cross-border financing must apply IFRS as endorsed by the Ministry of Finance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: People's Republic of China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS / ASBE) – substantially IFRS converged; small and medium-sized enterprises may apply the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises (中小主体会计准则) if revenue below RMB 30 million and total assets below RMB 50 million; customs brokerage licensed operations are normally expected to adopt full CAS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing; however, under the Foreign Investment Law and the Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting, a WFOE must report beneficial owner and ultimate controlling party information as part of the annual foreign investment report filed with SAMR/MOFCOM within the January 1 – June 30 window. Any change in shareholders, beneficial owners, or ultimate controllers must be filed with the market regulation authority within 30 days from the date of change and, where exchange control is involved, reported to SAFE. The company register (shareholder register) must be updated concurrently. Failure to report a 30-day share transfer or ownership change triggers administrative penalties. The board of directors must also submit annual audit confirmation and disclose any ongoing UBO changes in the annual report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: RMB 12,000 – RMB 40,000 (USD 1,700 – USD 5,600) per annum depending on transaction volume and customs brokerage scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for qualified High-and-New-Technology Enterprises; 100% additional deduction for eligible R&D expenses (200% super-deduction policy); 10-year loss carryforward for qualified HTNE; small low-profit enterprise preferential CIT rates; tax super-deduction for wages of disabled staff; qualified technology transfer income exemption up to RMB 5 million; no general patent box in China; comprehensive bonded zone regional incentives may be applied if legally enacted, subject to anti-abuse review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (A class) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (e-Tax); supplementary schedules A105000, A107010, A109000 and relevant non-resident withholding forms are attached electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual closing return with quarterly provisional prepayment returns
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year-end (31 May for calendar-year taxpayers); quarterly provisional returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from customs clearance brokerage, bonded transit management, customs consulting and ancillary logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report on accrual basis and reconcile with the customs brokerage license transaction ledger, ACH/wire settlement records and VAT filing revenue. Any China-source service revenue of a foreign enterprise separately carried on by the WFOE must be excluded from the entity-level CIT gross income and handled under non-resident enterprise income tax withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible direct costs including licensed customs broker salaries, subcontractor customs clearance fees, bonded warehouse handling costs, transit security and operating leases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs actually incurred in generating taxed Chinese income are deductible. Payments to offshore related parties for alleged customs consulting or transit management services require real service substance, supporting contracts, invoices, business records and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business taxes and surcharges: urban construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, real estate tax, land use tax and vehicle tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Customs VAT and customs duties are not deductible as business taxes and surcharges. Fines and penalties levied by customs or tax authorities are never deductible. Non-resident withholding taxes on dividends, interest or royalties are also prohibited as deductions at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing expenses, client entertainment, overseas travel, telecommunications, sales commissions and promotional activities for customs brokerage services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entertainment expenses are limited to the lower of 60% of actual amounts and 0.5% of annual revenue; advertising and business promotion expenses are deductible up to 15% of revenue with excess carried forward. Third-party commission payments must be commercially justified and reported on factual beneficial owner details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office rents, legal and professional fees, compliance and AML program costs, insurance, licenses, depreciation, IT systems, board and management expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid by the WFOE to its foreign parent or offshore affiliates are not deductible under Article 10(e) EIT Law unless they are compensated for actual specific services, supported by contracts, function and risk analysis, and evidence that no double-charge occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on bank loans and intercompany borrowings, bank wire and ACH transaction fees, exchange gains/losses, guarantee fees and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related parties is subject to a 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization limit for general enterprises (5:1 for financial institutions). Excess interest is non-deductible and may be recharacterised as a dividend distribution subject to 10% withholding tax unless treaty relief is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Asset Impairment and Fair Value Changes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bad debt provisions, inventory valuation reserves, impairment of fixed assets, intangible assets and goodwill, and fair value losses on financial instruments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: General impairment provisions or expected credit losses are non-deductible for CIT unless actual loss has occurred and is evidenced. Specific bad debt loss may be deducted after exhausting legal collection remedies; also file an asset loss declaration under the annual CIT package.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from disposal of assets, donations received, fines, penalties, extraordinary losses, and charitable donations paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Donations to qualified charitable organisations are deductible up to 12% of accounting profit. Fines for customs or tax violations, administrative penalties and blacklisting sanctions are non-deductible. Interest on overdue taxes is deductible if paid? Interest on tax underpayment is non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before income tax determined under China Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point for the reconciliation schedule. If the WFOE is a customs broker, its licensed income should reconcile with national customs broker reporting systems; non-resident shareholders' own accounting profit does not enter this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit plus tax-add backs, less tax-exempt income, less deductible loss carryforward, and after special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: General tax loss carryforward is limited to five years; qualified high-tech enterprises may carry forward ten years. Losses from foreign parent or non-resident affiliates cannot be used by the Chinese WFOE. The loss carryforward amount must be itemised on schedule A106000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard CIT rate; 15% for qualified High-and-New-Technology Enterprises; 20% for small low-profit enterprises with effective reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate applies to the Chinese resident WFOE on its worldwide income. There is no consolidated or streaming tax filing with the non-resident parent. Non-resident persons are not taxed at this rate on Chinese-source dividends, interest, royalties, or services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 12 - Tax Payable at Entity Level
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable CIT rate before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the provisional entity-level CIT before all credits. For a WFOE with overseas branches, foreign-source income is included and foreign tax credits are computed separately; no shareholder-level tax is reflected here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 13 - Tax Credits and Preferential Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, R&D additional deduction, accelerated depreciation, venture capital investment credit, equipment purchase and qualified technology transfer income exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit is capped at the Chinese CIT allocable to foreign-source income. Taxes paid by a foreign parent or offshore shareholder cannot be credited against WFOE CIT. The R&D additional deduction requires contemporaneous project and personnel records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax due for the fiscal year after applying all credits and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is not the dividend withholding tax base. When the WFOE distributes profits to a non-resident shareholder, a separate 10% withholding tax is triggered, unless a reduced treaty rate is substantiated before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate quarterly CIT prepayments paid during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly prepayments are based on actual profit or prior-year benchmark. The WFOE should ensure the annual return reconciles with each quarter's payment vouchers, and any non-resident withholding credits from foreign-source dividends are not misreported in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 16 - Net Tax Payable or Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive amount means net tax payable upon filing; negative amount means refund or carryover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by the statutory deadline to avoid daily surcharges. Refund applications are audited for fraudulent customs brokerage invoices and VAT input schemes. Non-resident shareholders cannot offset their shareholder-level WHT against the WFOE's CIT overpayment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 administrative fine under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law; late payment: 0.05% daily interest surcharge plus compulsory seizure of assets; false or under-declared tax: 50% to 500% monetary penalty under Article 63; criminal tax evasion: where unpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of tax due, imprisonment up to seven years and fines under Article 201 of the Criminal Law; serious dishonest taxpayers are blacklisted under the Joint Punishment Memorandum, with travel restrictions and denial of customs brokerage license renewals.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax on outbound dividends paid by a Chinese enterprise to non-resident shareholders under EIT Law Article 3(3) and Article 27(5); treaty may reduce the rate to as low as 5% for a beneficial owner company holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital under many bilateral DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced treaty withholding, the WFOE as withholding agent must collect and file before payment: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the non-resident shareholder's home tax authority covering the year of dividend payment; (2) the treaty relief declaration form and beneficial ownership statement under SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60, and satisfying the beneficial ownership test of SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 - including substantive business activity, no conduit or back-to-back arrangement, and true entitlement to the dividend; (3) evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period required by the applicable treaty; (4) legal entity charts, board resolutions and audited financial statements supporting substance. If the reduced rate is not applied at payment time, the non-resident may apply to the competent Chinese tax authority for a refund within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise are subject to 10% statutory withholding tax on gross royalties sourced in China, treaty rates generally range from 5% to 10% for beneficial owners; interest paid to non-resident related lenders is subject to 10% statutory withholding tax, with most Chinese DTAs providing 10% or lower rates (often 5% to 10%) and certain government or financial-institution interest exemptions; interest on related-party debt exceeding the thin capitalisation ratio may be recharacterised as dividends and taxed at the dividend WHT rate without treaty benefit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 400 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 200 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transactions, or RMB 100 million for other related-party transactions; Master File mandatory where aggregate related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion; Country-by-Country Report required for a multinational group with consolidated annual revenue of RMB 5.5 billion or more; all documentation must be submitted within the statutory form-filling window and contemporaneously prepared.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form and the OECD-aligned Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) doctrine through EIT Law Article 47, Special Tax Adjustment Rules and treaty anti-abuse provisions. A customs brokerage WFOE must prove that it performs the functions, owns the assets and bears the risks of customs clearance and bonded transit management using its own licensed staff, physical premises, decision-making and Chinese bank accounts; shell companies with no real personnel or business activity are denied treaty benefits, profits are recharacterised as China-source service income or dividends, and the general anti-avoidance rule enables tax authority adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and False VAT Input Claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing CIT returns with fabricated customs brokerage expenses, fake logistics invoices, inflated staff compensation, duplicate bonded warehouse costs, or intentionally omitting taxable revenue from ACH/wire settlements; operating with dual sets of books and diverting brokerage fee income to shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Law Article 63 orders recovery of underpaid tax plus a penalty of 50% to 500% of the under-declared tax; daily late payment surcharge is 0.05%; false customs declarations are separately penalised under Customs Law sections on smuggling/false declaration; Criminal Law Article 201 imposes fines and imprisonment up to seven years when unpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 where directors or shareholders abuse limited liability, commingle personal and corporate funds, or transfer assets fraudulently; directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid CIT, VAT, customs duties and penalties; travel bans, high-consumption restrictions and blacklisting under the joint punishment system apply; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment from three to seven years and disqualification from serving as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, management fees, or service charges to a Hong Kong or offshore parent without real services or economic substance; entering into non-arm's-length long-term brokerage contracts with related logistics affiliates to strip Chinese profits; failing to prepare Local File/Master File despite exceeding RMB 400 million related-party tangible asset transfers or RMB 200 million intangible transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 41 requires arm's-length pricing and Article 48 authorises recharacterisation with a 10-year look-back period; Special Tax Adjustment Rules impose late interest and documentation penalties; unpaid tax can be recovered with a 50% to 500% fine under Tax Administration Law Article 63; recharacterised excess payments may be taxed as deemed dividends with 10% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign sham related-party transactions and defeat tax collection are personally liable for the adjusted tax, penalties and interest if the corporate form is used as a mere instrumentality; personal asset attachment and civil restitution orders may issue; tax authority blacklisting restricts cross-border travel; willful evasion can trigger Criminal Law Article 201 liability and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive DTA Relief, Shell Company, and AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a letterbox non-resident shareholder with no economic substance to claim a 5% treaty dividend rate instead of the statutory 10% WHT; operating the WFOE as an empty shell customs broker that merely channels brokerage fees and bonded transit payments without licensed operations; failing to identify beneficial owners in ACH/wire payment rails and deliberately structuring fee settlements to hide cross-border money movements or avoid AML reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DTA relief is denied under SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60 and Announcement 2018 No. 9 with full 10% WHT recaptured; automatic tax adjustments, late interest and a 50% to 500% false-declaration fine apply; AML Law violations subject the institution and responsible officers to monetary penalties; Criminal Law Article 191 on money laundering imposes imprisonment and confiscation of property; the customs brokerage licence may be revoked under customs administration rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or implement abusive treaty, shell-company and money-laundering structures are subject to civil restitution, joint and several liability for underwithheld tax, travel bans, court-ordered asset disgorgement, personal fines, and imprisonment from five to ten years in serious money-laundering cases; the corporate veil is pierced when the WFOE is an alter ego or sham device, exposing the director's personal assets.
